title: Homework 2 candidate: calibrated initial rates and inhibition evidence

questions.prompt: Using the compound_b product standards on day d01, convert a separate static signal of 35.0 arbitrary units to product concentration. Report a compatible concentration unit and exactly three significant figures.

At substrate 45 µM for compound_b, calculate each day's ordinary least-squares slope over 0, 2 and 4 seconds for reaction and its matched blank. Subtract the blank slope, divide by that day/condition's calibration gain, then average the four day rates. Report concentration per time with exactly three significant figures.

In a separately stipulated simple competitive model, Km is 15 µM, inhibitor concentration is 30 µM and Ki is 15 µM. Calculate Km,app=(1+[I]/Ki)Km. Report concentration with exactly two significant figures. These supplied model constants are not a fit to the displayed observations.

For vehicle day d01 at starting substrate 5 µM, calculate blank-corrected product accumulated from 0 to 4 seconds using the matched gain. Under the separately stipulated one-to-one substrate-to-product accounting, express that amount as a percent of the starting substrate concentration. Report a percent unit and exactly four significant figures.

Summarize the four independently prepared assay days after matched blank subtraction and day/condition calibration. Use only the 0, 2 and 4 second slope window. Upload exact columns condition,days,mean_rate_15_nm_s,mean_rate_135_nm_s with rows vehicle,compound_a,compound_b. Counts are exact; rate-cell tolerance is 0.005 nM/s. Time observations, substrate levels and calibration standards do not add independent assay days.
For vehicle d01 at 135 µM, compare the blank-corrected calibrated endpoint slope from 0 to 10 seconds with the ordinary least-squares slope over 0, 2 and 4 seconds.

response_fields.prompt: Report late endpoint slope divided by early slope as a bare dimensionless ratio. Report exactly 2 significant figures.
Which conclusion follows from this window comparison?
options: The later window proves irreversible inhibition at a named active-site residue.
The rate estimate depends on the window; curvature alone does not identify depletion, inactivation or another cause.
Every late endpoint is an initial rate when its time axis starts at zero.

questions.prompt: Select one response for each independent calibration, blank, replication and inference criterion.

response_fields.prompt: Which calibration should convert compound_b day d02 signal?
options: Vehicle standards pooled across days.
Compound_b product standards from day d02, subject to the stated linearity/matrix assumptions.
The compound_a curve at the highest substrate.

response_fields.prompt: How should background drift be handled before rate conversion?
options: Subtract the blank's initial offset only and ignore its slope.
Use the blank as extra independent enzyme replicates.
Subtract the same-day, same-condition, same-substrate no-enzyme slope in the selected window.

response_fields.prompt: What is the independent replicate unit in this construction?
options: Each separately prepared assay day, with conditions/substrates/time points paired within the day.
Every detector time point and standard is a separate biological replicate.
Each column in the input file.

response_fields.prompt: What does overlap with vehicle after calibrated blank correction support?
options: Proof that the compound has no molecular interaction under any condition.
Consistency with no resolved catalytic-rate difference in this synthetic assay; other effects need separate tests.
Proof of the compound's therapeutic safety.

questions.prompt: Select all statements justified by the stated single-substrate model and measurement limits. Scoring is two points times (correct options selected minus incorrect options selected) divided by the total number of correct options, clamped from zero to two.
options: A competitive-looking rate curve proves occupancy of the substrate-binding pocket.
An enzyme can speed approach to equilibrium without changing the reaction equilibrium constant.
A fluorescent product standard by itself measures the amount of active enzyme.
Km is always the substrate-binding dissociation constant.
With kcat and other model conditions fixed, doubling active enzyme concentration doubles Vmax.
